chapter: Idaho tours, Music Town and retirement
title: Taking a band to Shadowland in Idaho, 1935-38
summary: Spikes assembled a band with Hollywood McCoy for yearly engagements in Kimberly, Idaho, with dancers from Flying Down To Rio; afterwards he opened a nightclub that failed.

bands.name: Reb Spikes and His Majors and Minors Orchestra

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: '35...I'm going too far...'35 they sent for me to come up in Idaho and bring a band, and I had to get a band together, and I went up there, and I picked up one of my brother's piano players called "Hollywood" McCoy, the first colored boy I think born in Hollywood, 1912 or '13, and we went up there in '35, and we made such a hit with it we just had a...I just had a bunch of musicians, and they all were pretty good jazz merchants, you know, and we just called anything they'd play it whether they had music or not, so we stayed up there in '35, I think it was, and then they come back in '36, and they wanted us to come back and then '37 we went back again and then I think that was the year that they had the "Flying Down To Rio," and I took a couple of the dancers with me, and the old people and all of them used to come miles to see...they knew about the picture, "Flying Down To Rio," and they'd come to see these two kids do that...uh, you know...South American dance, and it just crowded them in, and this was in Shadowland in Kimberly, Iowa, and we went up there about three or four years, and when they come back in '38, I stayed home. I didn't go back, and then I worked around awhile and opened a nightclub and run it awhile and got out of that, couldn't make any money in it, and I was broke, and I sold all the records that I had brought out of the music store for nothing practically, and that... Some of those records now are very expensive 'cause they're the first records Jelly Roll made and wrote and Bessie Smith and all of those people.
